native_retrieval.title: These 2 Internet Service Providers Get Consumer Reports Top Scores - bgr.com
native_retrieval.snippet: There are many things to consider when deciding on what internet service to choose, but price and speed are among the top two. If you want to choose some of the best internet service providers (ISPs), here are the top two options according to Consumer Reports. Based on a 2025 survey of more than 73,000 people who were surveyed to discover what they liked and disliked about their internet providers, CR's list of Best and Worst Home Internet Providers determined that Greenlight Networks, was the top-rated ISP among customers, with second place going to EPB, or the Electric Power Board of Chattanooga. Among the dozens of ISPs available, ranking major internet providers worst to best is challenging, but CR's survey and rankings show how both companies took the top spots and how they compare to the competition. Another ISP that offers fiber internet and one that is second on Consumer Report's list for best and worst internet providers, is EPB.

native_retrieval.title: Tax Fraud Blotter: Took the internet by storm - Accounting Today
native_retrieval.snippet: **Miami**: A Florida man pleaded guilty to evading taxes on millions in income that he earned from business ventures that sold internet access to American servicemembers and contractors stationed abroad. Between 2013 and 2018, Joseph Stewart, of Miami, earned more than $4.5 million in dividends from his 50% ownership in a business that sold internet access to American servicemembers and contractors stationed at Kandahar Airfield, Afghanistan. Between 2013 and 2018, Stewart also earned income from his 50% ownership of a separate business that sold internet access to soldiers stationed on Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. As a result of these false statements, the tax professionals drafted tax returns for Stewart for 2013 through 2020 that underreported his income and taxes due. Stewart filed these false returns with the IRS, except for a 2013 tax return, which reported that Stewart owed approximately $155,720 in taxes.

native_retrieval.title: Data centers drove $6.3B in PJM capacity auction costs: market monitor - Utility Dive
native_retrieval.snippet: In the PJM’s last four capacity auctions, data center-related capacity charges were nearly half of the $63.6 billion in total charges in that period, Monitoring Analytics says. * Data centers are responsible for $6.3 billion, or 38%, of the $16.4 billion in charges from the PJM Interconnection’s just-held capacity auction, Joseph Bowring, president of Monitoring Analytics, said in an email to Utility Dive. * In PJM’s last four base capacity auctions, data center-driven capacity charges totaled $29.4 billion — 46% of the $63.6 billion in total capacity charges in that period, Bowring said. Ratepayers in PJM are not only paying capacity charges for existing and potential data centers, they are paying for higher energy and transmission costs data centers have caused, according to Bowring. First, data centers and other large loads should contract for their own generation, according to a proposal the market monitor made last month as part of PJM’s fast-track stakeholder process for a backstop reliability auction.

native_retrieval.title: Watchdog report on Cook County tax tech contract: ‘Nobody’s hands are clean’ - Chicago Tribune
native_retrieval.snippet: Politics |   Watchdog report on Cook County tax tech…. # Watchdog report on Cook County tax tech contract: ‘Nobody’s hands are clean’. Cook County’s inspector general released a report Tuesday on the county’s troubled decade-long property tax system modernization, sharing some insiders’ candid — and wholly anonymous — reflections on what has gone wrong and estimating the county has so far spent $63 million on the project. The office reviewed the original contracts with Tyler Technologies and spoke to leaders of the county’s property tax offices and company officials from Tyler and two other contractors later brought on to provide oversight and project management. Per office policy, the IG does not name the subjects of investigations, but the findings in Tuesday’s report echo an investigation into cost overruns and intra-office strife by the Tribune and Injustice Watch involving different Tyler contracts, as well as Tribune reporting over the past year on property tax problems.

Customers of Amazon Web Services received a rude shock ahead of the weekend as they received alerts showing massive bills from the cloud giant, some of which were in the billions and even trillions of US dollars. AWS customers posted screenshots of their billing dashboards, with some whose normal usage is in the tens of dollars per month being told that they would owe billions or even more. Datadog staff engineer and AWS Hero AJ Stuyvenberg was one of several AWS customers to share billing estimates. In February this year, AWS posted a rebuttal for a Cost Explorer incident reported by *Financial Times*, which took place in December last year, and which the publication attributed to artificial intelligence and the Kiro coding agent.

native_retrieval.title: Waukegan clears way for 7G internet service: ‘I want it’ - Chicago Tribune
native_retrieval.snippet: Lake County News-Sun |   Waukegan clears way for 7G internet service: ‘I…. # Waukegan clears way for 7G internet service: ‘I want it’. People in Waukegan looking for a fiberoptic internet connection with a high-speed 7G connection accommodating multiple devices and simultaneous users, or someone who needs an introductory plan meeting their basic needs, will have a new opportunity to find it. Tony Signporella, the director of government relations for Clearwave Fiber, said at a meeting of the City Council’s Public Works & Infrastructure Committee on June 15 that the company plans to build an underground fiberoptic network to accommodate 9,000 homes and 2,300 businesses. “We want to give the residents a choice for fast and reliable internet service,”  Signporella said. The Waukegan City Council unanimously approved a master right-of-way agreement between the city and Clearwave Fiber on Monday at City Hall without debate, giving the company the right to create its fiberoptic network.

english_retrieval.title: America Movil agrees to acquire Peru broadband provider Wow - Developing Telecoms
english_retrieval.snippet: ## America Movil agrees to acquire Peru broadband provider Wow. America Movil has agreed to acquire Peruvian fixed broadband provider Wow from Liberty Latin America and its partners, strengthening the operator's position in Peru's growing fibre broadband market. Liberty Latin America said its stake in Wow, along with those of its investment partners, will be sold to America Movil Peru, the local subsidiary of Mexico-based telecoms giant America Movil. Wow operates primarily as a fixed broadband internet service provider in Peru. Liberty Latin America first acquired a minority stake in the company in 2021 and has made further investments since then, with the business accounted for as an equity method investment. The company said the sale forms part of its strategy to rationalise its operating portfolio and optimise capital allocation across its business. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including approval from Peru's competition authority, the National Institute for the Defense of Competition and Protection of Intellectual Property (INDECOPI).

english_retrieval.title: Prof. Shlomo Mashiach, pioneer of in vitro fertilization in Israel, dies at 89 - Ynetnews
english_retrieval.snippet: Shlomo Mashiach, pioneer of in vitro fertilization in Israel, dies at 89. Professor Shlomo Mashiach, one of the pioneers of in vitro fertilization in Israel and who by his own estimate helped bring approximately 40,000 babies into the world, has died at the age of 89 in Tel Aviv. Mashiach was among the founders of the Faculty of Medicine at Tel Aviv University and formerly headed the Women's and Maternity Hospital at Sheba Medical Center in Tel Hashomer. His sons told Ynet that his home in Tel Aviv was directly hit by an Iranian missile during Operation 'With Courage.' A few months later, he ran to the safe room during air raid sirens and was injured, which led to a deterioration in his condition.
